title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2026
short_title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would fix minor errors and clarify the original policy intent of veterans' compensation and rehabilitation reforms before they take effect on 1 July 2026.

It would amend the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act, the Veterans' Entitlements Act and the Defence-related Claims Act through ten changes, including allowing the Veterans' Review Board to notify the Chief of Defence Force when a serving member seeks review.
The government says the bill has no financial impact and was developed from consultation between 2022 and 2024.
changes: Allow the Veterans' Review Board to tell the Chief of Defence Force when a serving member applies for review, so the CDF can become a party and be told the outcome.
Remove the requirement that applications for travel expenses related to the Board be communicated to the Board.
Clarify that dependants who already received compensation before 1 July 2026 do not need to retest eligibility after that date.
Confirm that the high rate of funeral compensation under the MRCA is available even if the low-rate criteria are also met.

Clarify that liability can be accepted for unintended outcomes of treatment given by the Australian Defence Force during service, and for treatment provided by the Department of Veterans' Affairs for an earlier service injury or disease.
Confirm that Victoria Cross Allowance and Decoration Allowance are excluded income for means testing and rate calculations.
summary.affected: Veterans, their dependants, serving members, the Veterans' Review Board, the Chief of Defence Force, and the Repatriation Commission.

divisions.question: The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-02-04.149.2) to the usual second reading text, which is "*that the bill be read a second time*" (parliamentary jargon for a agreeing with the main idea of the bill). ### Amendment text > *That the amendment moved by the honourable member for Hume be agreed to:* > > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > >> *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House calls on the Government to remove any references to a notification of the Chief of the Defence Force, considering the impact this would have on a member's right to privacy and access to care".*

speeches.speaker: Matt Keogh
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of legislation making technical amendments to support the Veterans' Entitlements, Treatment and Support (Simplification and Harmonisation) Act 2025 and its transition to a single veterans entitlement framework from 1 July 2026, stating that existing payments and benefits would continue uninterrupted.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that the Copyright Amendment Bill 2025, Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2025 and Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework Bill) 2025 stand referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: Moved an amendment to the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill seeking removal of references to notification of the Chief of the Defence Force, citing privacy and access to care; supported the bill's transition to a single framework operating from 1 July 2026 and called for a Senate inquiry.

speeches.speaker: Claire Clutterham
speeches.brief: Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2025, describing technical changes needed to implement a single MRCA framework from 1 July 2026 and simplify compensation, rehabilitation, healthcare and education entitlements for veterans and their families.

speeches.speaker: Matt Keogh
speeches.brief: Moved an amendment to remove item 44 of schedule 1 from the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2025, concerning notifications about non-liability health care. Said the issue would be reconsidered, and reported that the amendment and bill as amended were agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2025 as necessary to implement a single compensation and rehabilitation system from 1 July 2026, while criticising the need for a second technical bill and opposing mandatory notification of the Chief of the Defence Force when serving members seek review or healthcare.
